definitions.explanation: A horizontal or vertical line of text in writing, printing, or on a screen. Used when referring to specific positions in documents, code, or printed material.
A row of the Japanese syllabary chart (五十音図), grouping kana that share the same consonant.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}の{行|ぎょう}を{読|よ}んでください。
この{文章|ぶんしょう}は{全部|ぜんぶ}で{何行|なんぎょう}ありますか。
examples.english: How many lines does this passage have in total?

examples.japanese: {三|さん}{行目|ぎょうめ}の{最初|さいしょ}の{単語|たんご}に{誤|あやま}りがあるので、{修正|しゅうせい}してください。
examples.english: There is an error in the first word on the third line, so please correct it.

examples.japanese: 「か」は{何行|なにぎょう}ですか。
{五十音図|ごじゅうおんず}の{各行|かくぎょう}には{五|いつ}つのかなが{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Each row of the kana chart has five kana lined up.

examples.japanese: 「さ{行|ぎょう}」には「さ・し・す・せ・そ」の{五|いつ}つの{音|おん}が{含|ふく}まれる。
examples.english: The 'sa row' includes the five sounds 'sa, shi, su, se, so.'

notes:
Read as ぎょう, this word refers to a line of text or a row in a chart. Do not confuse with other readings of the same kanji: {行|い}く (to go), {行|おこな}う (to carry out), or {行|こう} (used in compounds like {銀行|ぎんこう}).

As a counter, {行|ぎょう} counts lines of text: {一行|いちぎょう} (one line), {二行|にぎょう} (two lines), {三行|さんぎょう} (three lines). The suffix {行目|ぎょうめ} specifies the ordinal position: {一行目|いちぎょうめ} (first line).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行|ぎょう}を{変|か}える: to start a new line
- {行|ぎょう}{間|かん}: line spacing
- {空白行|くうはくぎょう}: blank line
- {行|ぎょう}{番号|ばんごう}: line number
- {改行|かいぎょう}: line break; new line

KANA CHART USAGE:
In the {五十音図|ごじゅうおんず}, each consonant group is called a {行|ぎょう}: {あ行|あぎょう}, {か行|かぎょう}, {さ行|さぎょう}, etc. Each column is called a {段|だん} (だん): {あ段|あだん}, {い段|いだん}, etc.
